title: The Two Witnesses
overview: Revelation chapter 11 presents a vivid prophetic vision focusing on the measuring of God's temple, the ministry and martyrdom of two powerful witnesses, and the ultimate triumph of God's kingdom. The chapter begins with the angel instructing John to measure the temple and altar, symbolizing God's protection and judgment. The two witnesses prophesy for 1,260 days, empowered with miraculous abilities, yet they face opposition and death by the beast from the abyss. Their resurrection and ascension inspire fear and reverence, followed by a great earthquake that leads many to glorify God. The chapter concludes with the sounding of the seventh trumpet, heralding God's eternal reign and the opening of His heavenly temple. This chapter emphasizes God's sovereignty, the certainty of prophetic testimony, and the final victory of Christ over evil.
structure:
**Verses 1-2: The Measuring of the Temple.** John is given a reed to measure the temple of God, the altar, and worshippers, but the outer court is left to the Gentiles, who will trample the holy city for forty-two months. This sets the stage for God's protection and judgment.

**Verses 3-6: The Ministry and Power of the Two Witnesses.** The two witnesses, described as olive trees and candlesticks, prophesy clothed in sackcloth for 1,260 days. They possess divine powers to judge and protect, including shutting heaven, turning waters to blood, and sending plagues.

**Verses 7-10: The Death and Mockery of the Witnesses.** After their testimony, the beast from the abyss kills them. Their bodies lie in the street of the spiritually corrupt city where Christ was crucified. The world rejoices over their death, celebrating their torment of the earth's inhabitants.

**Verses 11-14: The Resurrection and Ascension of the Witnesses.** After three and a half days, God breathes life into them, and they stand, causing fear. They ascend to heaven in a cloud as their enemies watch. A great earthquake follows, killing many and prompting the survivors to glorify God.

**Verses 15-19: The Seventh Trumpet and God's Reign.** The seventh angel sounds, proclaiming the kingdoms of the world have become Christ’s. The elders worship God, acknowledging His eternal power and judgment. The temple in heaven opens, revealing the ark of the covenant amid thunder, lightning, and hail, symbolizing God's presence and judgment.

keyVerses.text: And I will give power unto my two witnesses, and they shall prophesy a thousand two hundred and threescore days, clothed in sackcloth.
keyVerses.significance: This verse introduces the two witnesses and their prophetic mission, highlighting their divine empowerment and the period of their testimony, which is central to understanding the chapter's prophetic timeline and God's sovereign plan.

keyVerses.text: And when they shall have finished their testimony, the beast that ascendeth out of the bottomless pit shall make war against them, and shall overcome them, and kill them.
keyVerses.significance: This verse reveals the opposition the witnesses face from the beast, symbolizing evil's temporary victory over God's servants, underscoring the reality of spiritual conflict and martyrdom in God's redemptive plan.

keyVerses.text: And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them.
keyVerses.significance: The resurrection of the witnesses demonstrates God's power over death and serves as a powerful testimony to all, inspiring fear and reverence, affirming the hope of resurrection for believers.

keyVerses.text: And the seventh angel sounded; and there were great voices in heaven, saying, The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ; and he shall reign for ever and ever.
keyVerses.significance: This verse proclaims the ultimate triumph of Christ's kingdom over all earthly powers, marking the fulfillment of God's sovereign rule and the consummation of history.

keyVerses.text: And the temple of God was opened in heaven, and there was seen in his temple the ark of his testament: and there were lightnings, and voices, and thunderings, and an earthquake, and great hail.
keyVerses.significance: The opening of the heavenly temple and the appearance of the ark symbolize God's presence and covenant faithfulness, accompanied by powerful signs of divine judgment and authority.

characters.name: The Two Witnesses
characters.description: Prophetic figures empowered by God to prophesy for 1,260 days, performing miracles and calling people to repentance. They symbolize faithful testimony amidst persecution and are ultimately martyred but resurrected and glorified.

characters.name: The Beast from the Bottomless Pit
characters.description: A demonic adversary who wages war against the two witnesses, kills them, and represents the forces of evil opposing God's kingdom and persecuting His people.

characters.name: God
characters.description: The sovereign Lord who empowers the witnesses, executes judgment, raises the dead, and establishes His eternal kingdom, demonstrating ultimate authority and faithfulness.

characters.name: The Twenty-Four Elders
characters.description: Heavenly beings who worship God following the seventh trumpet, representing the redeemed community and affirming God's reign and justice.

themes.description: The chapter highlights God's judgment through the measuring of the temple, the witnesses' plagues, the earthquake, and the wrath of God, emphasizing His righteous authority over all creation.
The two witnesses embody faithful proclamation and suffering for the gospel, illustrating the cost of obedience and the power of God's word even in the face of death.
The resurrection and ascension of the witnesses affirm God's power over death and the ultimate victory of His kingdom, offering hope to believers.
From measuring the temple to the sounding of the seventh trumpet, God's sovereign control over history and His eternal reign are central, assuring believers of His ultimate plan.

historicalContext: Revelation was written in the late first century AD, during a time of intense persecution of Christians under Roman imperial authority. The imagery of the temple and the holy city reflects Jerusalem’s significance as the center of Jewish worship and the site of Christ’s crucifixion. The reference to Gentiles trampling the holy city for forty-two months corresponds to a period of tribulation and suffering, possibly reflecting Roman oppression. The two witnesses may symbolize faithful Jewish and Gentile testimony or specific prophetic figures, set against the backdrop of apocalyptic conflict between good and evil. The political climate was marked by tension between the early church and imperial powers, making the message of divine sovereignty and ultimate victory especially poignant.

theologicalInterpretations.description: This perspective interprets the two witnesses as representing the faithful church or prophetic ministry throughout church history, with the 1,260 days symbolizing a long period of trial and testimony. The beast is seen as oppressive political powers opposing God's people.

Futurists understand the two witnesses as literal individuals who will prophesy during a future tribulation period immediately preceding Christ’s return. The beast is a future antichrist figure who kills them, emphasizing end-time events.

Preterists see the witnesses as symbolic of the faithful Jewish remnant or early Christian prophets during the first century, with the beast representing Roman imperial forces. The events are largely fulfilled in the past, near the time of the destruction of Jerusalem.

crossReferences.connection: The two olive trees and candlesticks imagery in Revelation 11 echoes Zechariah’s vision, symbolizing God’s anointed servants who stand before Him.
The period of forty-two months corresponds to the time of persecution and oppression described in Daniel, linking Old Testament prophecy with Revelation’s timeline.
Jesus’ teaching on persecution and the endurance of the saints parallels the witnesses’ ministry and suffering in Revelation 11.
Jesus’ declaration as the resurrection and the life connects to the resurrection of the two witnesses, affirming God’s power over death.
The imagery of thunder, lightning, and hail in Revelation 11:19 reflects the psalmist’s depiction of God’s majestic and fearful presence.

application: Remain faithful in witness even amid opposition, trusting God’s power to sustain and vindicate.
Recognize the reality of spiritual conflict and pray for protection and boldness in proclaiming the gospel.
Take comfort in the resurrection hope and God’s ultimate victory over evil and death.
Worship God as sovereign King, acknowledging His authority over all earthly kingdoms.
Be encouraged to persevere during trials, knowing God’s judgment and justice will prevail.
Reflect on the importance of measuring one’s spiritual life by God’s standards, seeking holiness and worship.
conclusion: Revelation 11 powerfully portrays the tension between faithful witness and hostile opposition, culminating in divine vindication and the establishment of God’s eternal kingdom. The two witnesses exemplify courage and perseverance in proclaiming God’s truth despite persecution, while their resurrection and ascension affirm the hope of life beyond death. The chapter’s vivid imagery of judgment, worship, and cosmic authority reminds believers that God remains sovereign over history, calling His people to steadfast faith and worship. For Christians today, this chapter encourages endurance, bold testimony, and confident hope in Christ’s ultimate reign.
timeline: c. AD 95-96 - Late First Century, during the reign of Emperor Domitian

outline.heading: Measuring the Temple and the Holy City
outline.description: John is instructed to measure the temple and altar, symbolizing God's protection of His people, while the outer court is given over to Gentile control, indicating a period of tribulation.

outline.heading: The Ministry and Power of the Two Witnesses
outline.description: The two witnesses prophesy for 1,260 days with divine authority to perform miracles and bring plagues, representing God's faithful testimony amidst opposition.

outline.heading: Death and Mockery of the Witnesses
outline.description: The beast kills the witnesses, and their bodies lie exposed in the city where Christ was crucified, while the world rejoices over their demise, illustrating the rejection of God's message.

outline.heading: Resurrection and Ascension of the Witnesses
outline.description: After three and a half days, God resurrects the witnesses who ascend to heaven, followed by a great earthquake that leads many to glorify God, demonstrating divine vindication.

outline.heading: The Seventh Trumpet and God's Sovereign Reign
outline.description: The sounding of the seventh trumpet announces Christ’s eternal kingdom, prompting worship from the elders and revealing God's presence in heaven with powerful signs of judgment.
